new_symbol_range_suggestions.sensor_activation_scale: positive; chosen so sensor_activation_scale*C is small at resting calcium but can become order one during ordinary pulses, allowing weak low-C activation and stronger curvature at moderate C

derivation_notes: The refinement keeps the calcium balance law for C unchanged and instead re-derives inhibitory-sensor loading with a saturating calcium occupancy factor. Using k_sensor_activation*C/(1 + sensor_activation_scale*C) as the effective activation flux captures omitted multistep or cooperative sensor binding while preserving the parent as a small-saturation-scale limit.
change_summary: The parent assumed a single linear calcium sensitivity for inhibitory-sensor activation. The successor replaces that with a saturating calcium-dependent activation coefficient, altering how H builds up across weak versus moderate calcium excursions and thereby changing the delayed feedback seen in C.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Sensor activation rate is linear in free calcium concentration with one fixed slope and no intrinsic curvature or threshold-like occupancy effect.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Cooperative calcium binding or multistep occupancy in the inhibitory sensor, causing nonlinear accumulation of the active inhibitory fraction as calcium rises.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered when sensor_activation_scale = 0, because the refined activation term (k_sensor_activation*C*(1 - H))/(1 + sensor_activation_scale*C) reduces exactly to k_sensor_activation*C*(1 - H).

response_change.parent_relation: The inhibitory sensor activates with a linear calcium dependence k_sensor_activation*C*(1-H), so at fixed H the suppression pathway strength grows with a single low-calcium slope and no intrinsic activation threshold curvature.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the linear calcium dependence of sensor activation by a steeper saturating calcium dependence so that inhibition accumulates weakly at very low C and disproportionately faster once C reaches a moderate activation range.
response_change.observable_effect: Across fixed stimulus_strength with identical initial conditions, low-amplitude calcium elevations produce less inhibition buildup than in the parent, while moderate elevations trigger earlier and stronger delayed suppression, changing pulse width and the onset of oscillation termination.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when C traverses a low-to-moderate range during transients or oscillations, so that sensor activation is neither always near zero nor always fully saturated; especially when stimulus_strength is large enough for CICR to lift C into this regime but clearance and inactivation still terminate excursions.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the same mechanism changes how H accumulates during ordinary calcium pulses; in holdout, the contrast extends to stronger pulses where the steeper activation curvature produces earlier shutdown and altered oscillation envelopes.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: The parent law is recovered in the limit where the refined sensor-activation nonlinearity reduces to linear dependence on C over the sampled range.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Nonlinear calcium occupancy of the inhibitory sensor
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Cooperative calcium binding or multistep occupancy in the inhibitory sensor, causing nonlinear accumulation of the active inhibitory fraction as calcium rises.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the effective activation coefficient of the inhibitory pathway now depends on the evolving state C, introducing response curvature that a single constant k_sensor_activation cannot reproduce across weak and moderate pulses.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Sensor activation rate is linear in free calcium concentration with one fixed slope and no intrinsic curvature or threshold-like occupancy effect.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The inhibitory sensor has saturating calcium-dependent occupancy, so its activation coefficient depends on the current calcium level.
evolution_contract.before_fragment: (k_release*stimulus_strength*(1 - H))/(1 + release_inactivation_scale*C) + (k_cicr_release*stimulus_strength*C*(1 - H))/(1 + release_inactivation_scale*C) - (k_extrusion*C)/(1 + pump_saturation_scale*C) - (k_buffer_bind*C*(1 - B))/(1 + buffer_binding_scale*C) + k_buffer_unbind*B
evolution_contract.after_fragment: (k_release*stimulus_strength*(1 - H))/(1 + release_inactivation_scale*C) + (k_cicr_release*stimulus_strength*C*(1 - H))/(1 + release_inactivation_scale*C) - (k_extrusion*C)/(1 + pump_saturation_scale*C) - (k_buffer_bind*C*(1 - B))/(1 + buffer_binding_scale*C) + k_buffer_unbind*B
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered exactly when sensor_activation_scale = 0, or approximately when sensor_activation_scale*C << 1 throughout the sampled trajectories.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Vary stimulus_strength while holding all other parameters and initial conditions fixed. Under weaker stimuli that keep C low, H accumulates less than in the parent; under stronger stimuli that lift C into the moderate activation range, H builds more abruptly and shuts release down earlier. This altered H trajectory feeds back onto the release terms and changes the scored dC_dt mapping across conditions through delayed inhibition, not merely an auxiliary unobserved branch.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set can only rescale the linear activation slope k_sensor_activation in dH_dt. That cannot simultaneously match weak-response underactivation and moderate-response sharper feedback onset across the stated conditions, because the child introduces calcium-dependent curvature in the inhibitory-loading law rather than a uniform gain change.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when C traverses a low-to-moderate range during transients or oscillations, so that sensor activation is neither always near zero nor always fully saturated; especially when stimulus_strength is large enough for CICR to lift C into this regime but clearance and inactivation still terminate excursions.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the same mechanism changes how H accumulates during ordinary calcium pulses; in holdout, the contrast extends to stronger pulses where the steeper activation curvature produces earlier shutdown and altered oscillation envelopes.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: The parent law is recovered in the limit where the refined sensor-activation nonlinearity reduces to linear dependence on C over the sampled range.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The inhibitory sensor is assumed to respond proportionally to cytosolic calcium at all low-to-moderate concentrations, omitting the common cooperative or saturating occupancy needed to represent a delayed feedback branch with a sharper calcium sensitivity.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Sensor activation rate is linear in free calcium concentration with one fixed slope and no intrinsic curvature or threshold-like occupancy effect.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Cooperative calcium binding or multistep occupancy in the inhibitory sensor, causing nonlinear accumulation of the active inhibitory fraction as calcium rises.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's linear sensor-activation law rather than adding a new process. The parent target mapping from observed states to dC_dt uses H as the only delayed inhibitor, but H itself is generated from a single-slope calcium response. Vary stimulus_strength while holding all other parameters and initial conditions fixed. In the parent, stronger stimuli mainly scale the amplitude and duration of C excursions, and H accumulation follows proportionally because dH_dt has no activation curvature beyond the (1-H) occupancy factor. In a child with cooperative or saturating calcium dependence of sensor activation, small calcium excursions generated under weaker stimulus produce noticeably less H buildup than predicted by the parent, whereas moderate excursions generated under stronger stimulus cross into a steeper activation range and suppress release sooner. This changes the scored mapping indirectly but consequentially through H, because the observed dC_dt at the same C and H trajectory history now comes from a differently curved H evolution that feeds back onto release. The contrast is scientifically admissible when calcium pulses reach the sensor's activation range; if C stays uniformly tiny or uniformly very high, the refinement becomes hard to distinguish. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot generally match both weak-response underactivation and moderate-response sharp feedback onset across those conditions, because changing k_sensor_activation only rescales one linear slope instead of introducing the needed curvature.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make the coefficient of an existing process depend on a declared quantity.

scenario_text: A constant upstream receptor stimulus drives calcium release into the cytosol while pumps remove calcium from the cytosol. A calcium-sensitive inhibitory sensor gradually becomes active and suppresses further release, creating delayed negative feedback. Cytosolic calcium and the inhibitory sensor are evolved together to study transient pulses and sustained oscillations.
